theme: relational visual reasoning, public images and recent literature
question: Have models reasoned over inscription groups as Bonta does, what public non-journal evidence has been considered, and which recent papers were actually reviewed?
outcome: Located prior selected relational image comparisons and larger transcription tasks, but no completed group-image inference benchmark. Audited use of community, public research, museum, independent-project and journalistic sources. Inspected four public photographs. Literal prefixes H97-3433 and H2001-5082 appear in one and two Lipi face-record lines respectively. Rakhigarhi's publicly photographed elephant sealing remains an unresolved object lead. Listed fourteen recent substantive or comparative works with reading depth, including abstract-only and version-specific access.
challenge: Scattered images lack complete accession, date and orientation metadata; recent uploads can reproduce older material. Direct image requests failed with 403/429. Literal prefixes do not complete object concordances. Full recent-paper review cannot be inferred from metadata access.
remedy: Used browser-visible pixels, preserved source URLs and authored observations, separated object/photo/post dates and actual acquisition depth, and implemented an aggregate-only identifier check with hashed inputs. No corpus edits or new model accuracy claim.
retry_when: Object registration/locus and catalogue joins can resolve the Rakhigarhi lead; a versioned public-image inventory and withheld object families can support a preregistered relational visual reasoning test.
